DE-FE0032254 Executive Summary The project objective was to develop high-capacity structured sorbent capable of achieving low CO 2 removal from air. The approach was divided into 2 primary activities: 1. Develop a direct air capture (DAC) sorbent that achieves the following key attributes: a. High CO loading capacity (>5 wt% CO ) – lower operating cost for sorbent regeneration 2 2 and capital cost by reducing the size of the DAC contactor/number of DAC module b. High Stability (<5% capacity fade over 100 adsorption-regeneration cycles) – lower operating costs for sorbent make-up c. High CO adsorption rate (>0.03 gmolCO /gSorbent-min) – lower capital cost by reducing 2 2 DAC contactor size/number of DAC modules 2. Develop and demonstrate a structured sorbent that achieves the following key attributes: a. Low cost of structured sorbent manufacturing b. High DAC sorbent loading capacity on structured substrate – lower operating cost for sorbent regeneration and lower capital cost by reducing size of DAC contactor/number of modules c. Capable of direct Joule-heated sorbent regeneration – reduce operating costs through efficient use of available electricity d. Utilize existing manufacturing infrastructure for rapid scale-up The DAC sorbent framework consists of an amine-functionalized onto hydrophobic polymer backbone with an added promoter. The functionalized amine provides high CO capacity and adsorption rates and the 2 polymer backbone to reduce water uptake. For the DAC sorbent development, multiple functionalized amines and promoters were assessed to select a candidate that achieved high CO capacity, high adsorption 2 rate, and high stability, as per the targets listed above. A key focus of the DAC sorbent screening was to determine a candidate that achieves high oxidative stability, as the primary mechanism for the degradation of amine-based sorbents is the oxidation of the functionalized amine when transitioning from high temperature regeneration to CO adsorption from air. From this work, a DAC sorbent, named ECCOsorb- 2 T1, was identified and used for the structured sorbent development.
